- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.75) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by rapid decline (e.g., >80 → <70), apply downward correction of 5–10% to subsequent days.  
- If forecast mean is >10% above true mean over 30d, apply mean reversion bias: subtract 1.5–3x the deviation from forecast mean.  
- When sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) after a peak, model often fails to adjust quickly; reduce forecast by 3–7% for next 3–5 days.  
- If forecast lags true trend by 2+ days (e.g., true drops while forecast still rising), apply lag correction: subtract 1–3% per lag day.  
- For sentiment history with alternating highs/lows, model overfits short-term momentum; dampen forecast volatility by 20–40% in next 5 days.
